figmaBuildPlan.tokenProfileHint: Use default enterprise-safe typography (Plus Jakarta Sans headings, Inter body) with Zoho Workplace mapped to warmth-people palette: primary #5c4ef5 and accent #f97316. Keep hero dark/brand-forward only if needed, but maintain strong white text contrast. Trust signals should be logo-first and dominant.

sections.variantHint: Enterprise hero with strong headline, subheadline, supporting line, side-by-side CTAs, and a dominant trust/logo strip directly below; no extra lead magnet; no form in hero.
sections.notes: Use a split hero layout if a product UI visual is available; otherwise keep text-led and centered within a strong brand background. Prevent headline overlap into full hero section by constraining text container width and using the 16+ word hero font rule. Include primary CTA and secondary CTA side by side with 16px gap. Keep supporting line as a concise utility row. Ensure hero is fully visible on initial load and scrollable content continues below.

sections.frameName: Trust Bar / Logos and Social Proof
sections.variantHint: Logo-first trust strip with badge, customer count stat, and divider-separated items on a light grey background.
sections.notes: This is the dominant trust signal. Prioritize a horizontal logo/badge row and customer count stat. Use a light grey band to separate from hero. If true logos are not supplied, use badge-style placeholders only as structured logo slots, not decorative cards. Keep it compact and highly legible.

sections.frameName: Feature Section / Why Choose Zoho Workplace
sections.variantHint: 4-feature card block arranged as 2-column grid on desktop, white cards with border and padding.
sections.notes: Do not use a nested grid inside a grid. Use a single readable card grid with 4 items, each card containing title and description only. Keep clean spacing and consistent card height. White background for contrast after trust strip.

sections.variantHint: 4-feature card block arranged as 2-column grid on desktop, with stronger descriptive lead-in and business-value framing.
sections.notes: Present the section as a continuation of value proposition, but maintain the same card system for consistency. Avoid inventing icons if none are provided; use text-first cards with optional small utility icon areas if required by the design system. Keep copy aligned to enterprise productivity and scale.

sections.variantHint: Integration category cards, 2-column or staggered 2-up list on desktop for readable scanning.
sections.notes: Use a clear list-card structure instead of dense multi-column grids. Group integration categories as separate cards with category title and comma-separated app examples. Keep this section highly scannable and avoid overcomplication. White background remains appropriate.

figmaExecutionNotes: Keep the top strip fixed only if included as an announcement/utility bar; otherwise do not introduce new sticky UI.
Do not add pricing, testimonials, form, news, or footer because they are not supported by the provided content map.
Use a full-page document flow so the page is scrollable beyond hero immediately.
Maintain one consistent feature card system across all feature sections; do not introduce nested grids or overly decorative layouts.
Use mobile as stacked single-column sections with CTA buttons stacked full-width and trust logos compressed into a scrollable or wrapped row.
Do not add any extra lead magnet module.
Ensure all section titles and descriptions match the provided content exactly and do not rewrite meaning.
Keep hero headline typography reduced for the 17-word headline to avoid overflow while preserving emphasis.
Trust section must remain the strongest social proof area; prioritize logo and customer-count prominence over all other secondary trust elements.

accentVisuals: Floating module cards for Mail, Cliq, Writer, Sheet, and Calendar
Trust badge strip with 'Trusted by 100,000+ Businesses Globally'
Tiny enterprise logo chips and UI microcards
heroStrategy.headline: Elevate Your Team’s Productivity with Zoho Workplace
heroStrategy.subheadline: A Complete Email & Collaboration Suite for Enterprises that Facilitates Unified Communication.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a full-bleed editorial hero with a strong white base, layered abstract workspace cards, and orange-red brand accents. Keep the composition asymmetrical and premium: headline centered-left with overlapping trust chips, while the right side is replaced by a stacked product constellation instead of a standard screenshot. Follow with alternating feature sections that switch light/dark backgrounds, include at least one deep dark proof section with light text, and add decorative grid lines and gradient orbs in the hero plus one supporting section. Avoid lifestyle imagery; use polished UI surfaces, SVG logo proof, and compact enterprise trust markers to make the page feel credible, organized, and senior-designed.

repetitionBreakers: Hero is content-first and editorial rather than a standard split hero
Trust appears immediately after hero as a logo band to satisfy logos-first strategy
Product section uses spotlight-plus-grid instead of a static feature grid
Pricing is compressed into a highlighted card rather than a comparison table
Testimonials use a carousel to change rhythm from the proof/logo section
Lead form becomes a floating card to create a distinct ending gesture
blueprint.pageTitle: Zoho Workplace for Enterprise Email and Collaboration
blueprint.metaDescription: Zoho Workplace is an enterprise email and collaboration suite that unifies communication, documents, chat, and meetings for productive teams. Explore features, trusted logos, pricing, and a clear next step.

sections.backgroundTreatment: editorial geometry with layered product modules, floating trust chips, and subtle precision-line framing
sections.designNote: Use a content-first hero that answers what it is, who it is for, and what to do next. Keep the headline large and direct, place the subheadline immediately below, and use a compact bullet-benefit cluster for Easy Setup, Made in India, and 24x7 Support. The CTA must read 'Get Started' in solid accent red at 100% opacity. Add a right-side abstract enterprise workspace visual rather than a lifestyle image. This should feel dynamic and enterprise-ready while matching warm traffic expectations.

Place trust immediately after the hero as a prominent logo-led proof band. Use 3 to 6 recognizable customer logos if available; if not, fallback to a clean metric strip anchored by 'Trusted by 100,000+ Businesses Globally'. Keep it compact, high-contrast, and horizontal without marquee motion.

Break the page into three distinct product blocks rather than one generic feature grid. The first block should spotlight the main click-driving benefit: all-in-one workspace and real-time collaboration. The second block should use an alternating panel layout for business-scale communication, integrations, and customization. The third block should compress integration ecosystems into a compact multi-chip or mini-panel layout. Because there are 5+ features across sections, avoid flat static grids and instead alternate spotlight panels, stacked cards, and a compact visual rail. This section should visually oscillate between large lead panels and denser supporting modules.

Use a credibility-support section only if needed to reinforce purchase confidence, but keep it lighter than the product and proof sections. Present as a small icon-list or concise card-grid focused on guidance, migration help, and enterprise fit. Do not let this become a generic vendor-benefits block.

Create a focused pricing card rather than a comparison table. Include the included items as a compact checklist and keep the primary CTA as 'Get Started' in solid accent red. This should feel like the first conversion moment after the proof-led middle, not a cluttered pricing matrix.

Use a testimonial carousel because there are 4+ entries. Keep the slides short and operationally specific, emphasizing collaboration, productivity, and implementation ease. This should function as social reassurance rather than a long-form story wall.

End with a centered floating lead form that feels like a conversion endpoint, not an interruption. Keep the form minimal and clearly state the next step. The CTA remains 'Get Started' and should be full-width on mobile. No alternate button labels.

Do not include a news/media logo strip unless actual press logos are available. Since the trust strategy is already satisfied by customer logos and metrics, skip this section to keep the page focused.

blueprint.designPersonality: Efficient, credible, and modern enterprise software with a clean editorial rhythm; it should feel like a trusted productivity platform built for large teams, with logos and proof leading the narrative and orange-red brand energy used sparingly but decisively.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a polished abstract enterprise workspace visual: email, chat, documents, and calendar modules floating in layered cards, with subtle UI depth and branded red highlight accents. Avoid lifestyle photography. The proof section should lean on SVG logo strips and compact trust badges, since logos are the dominant trust signal.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is concise but enterprise-facing, so 56px gives strong presence without overwhelming the hero. It supports a premium B2B feel and keeps the layout stable on desktop.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Split hero with brand/logo on the left and a centered headline block below/adjacent; strong typographic hierarchy, short support line, and a compact bullet-benefit list. The reference favors a direct, single-message hero rather than a media-led narrative.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Top hero followed by a lead-capture form module, then stacked feature sections with consistent heading/description blocks and repeated benefit grids. Rhythm is linear and conversion-focused, with limited visual interruption.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Simple flat content cards/blocks with minimal ornamentation, likely bordered or lightly shadowed. Emphasis is on readable text density over decorative styling; icon usage is sparse or absent in the provided map.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary and secondary CTA pairing in the hero, with form-first conversion support immediately after. Secondary CTAs are used as low-friction alternatives; later sections de-emphasize CTAs and focus on feature explanation.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No visible pricing module in the reference pattern. If used in a similar layout, pricing should be introduced as a separate conversion section rather than embedded in the hero.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not represented in the provided reference excerpt; likely a standard informational footer rather than a conversion-heavy footer band.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Primarily text-led with logo treatment in the hero; no dominant image, video, or product mockup shown in the extracted pattern. Media usage is restrained and supportive rather than illustrative.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Stacked feature sections with label, headline, descriptive paragraph, and multi-item feature lists/grids. Content is organized in repeated modules that support long-form explanation and progressive disclosure through sectioning rather than accordions.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form card placed directly beneath the hero for fast conversion. Uses a framed container with headline, multiple hidden tracking fields, and visible user-input fields; form is presented as a separate conversion surface.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, low-motion presentation with no apparent animated storytelling; if animation exists, it is likely minimal and utility-focused rather than decorative.
designNotes: Prioritize conversion clarity over visual complexity.
Use a strong text hierarchy with concise supporting bullets.
Keep forms close to the hero for immediate lead capture.
Repeat a consistent section template for long content.
Avoid heavy motion, carousel dependence, or tabbed navigation in the core layout.
Use ample whitespace and restrained branding to maintain enterprise credibility.

blueprint.heroFormBgRule: MANDATORY: Use heroBackgroundVideo as full-bleed autoplay muted loop video behind everything

mustHaveMoments: Prominent hero with a clear product value proposition and compact benefit bullets
Dominant trust strip immediately after hero featuring business logos / scale proof
Single, readable feature story section without nested grids
Pricing/inclusion section with enterprise-ready plan details and migration support
Testimonial section to reinforce workflow, productivity, and ease of adoption
Persistent top CTA strip for quick conversion access across the page
Footer with complete navigation/support credibility elements
avoidPatterns: Do not add an extra lead magnet or secondary offer beyond the existing trial/get-started CTAs
Do not use grid inside grid layouts for feature content
Do not make the page hero-only; full page must be visible and scrollable
Do not hide or omit the form area if the page requires it, but do not invent one when not provided
Do not let headings overlap the full hero section
Do not mismatch section content with product messaging
Do not introduce loading states or layout issues that block scrolling
Do not omit the fixed top strip, CTA strip, or footer
designStrategy.reasoning: Zoho Workplace is a single-product enterprise landing page with long-form content and strong social proof potential. Since visitors trust logos most, the page should lead with proof from recognizable business adoption, then quickly connect that credibility to a clear productivity value proposition. The best structure is proof-led and conversion-focused: a split hero for clarity, a dominant trust band, readable stacked sections for features/integrations/insight, and a final pricing-plus-testimonial close. The design should feel efficient and enterprise-safe, with medium CTA pressure and balanced density to keep the page scannable without feeling sparse.

Desktop.variantHint: Enterprise hero with strong headline, subheadline, supporting line, side-by-side CTAs, and a dominant trust/logo strip directly below; no extra lead magnet; no form in hero.
Desktop.notes: Use a split hero layout if a product UI visual is available; otherwise keep text-led and centered within a strong brand background. Prevent headline overlap into full hero section by constraining text container width and using the 16+ word hero font rule. Include primary CTA and secondary CTA side by side with 16px gap. Keep supporting line as a concise utility row. Ensure hero is fully visible on initial load and scrollable content continues below.

Desktop.frameName: Trust Bar / Logos and Social Proof
Desktop.variantHint: Logo-first trust strip with badge, customer count stat, and divider-separated items on a light grey background.
Desktop.notes: This is the dominant trust signal. Prioritize a horizontal logo/badge row and customer count stat. Use a light grey band to separate from hero. If true logos are not supplied, use badge-style placeholders only as structured logo slots, not decorative cards. Keep it compact and highly legible.

Desktop.frameName: Feature Section / Why Choose Zoho Workplace
Desktop.variantHint: 4-feature card block arranged as 2-column grid on desktop, white cards with border and padding.
Desktop.notes: Do not use a nested grid inside a grid. Use a single readable card grid with 4 items, each card containing title and description only. Keep clean spacing and consistent card height. White background for contrast after trust strip.

Desktop.variantHint: 4-feature card block arranged as 2-column grid on desktop, with stronger descriptive lead-in and business-value framing.
Desktop.notes: Present the section as a continuation of value proposition, but maintain the same card system for consistency. Avoid inventing icons if none are provided; use text-first cards with optional small utility icon areas if required by the design system. Keep copy aligned to enterprise productivity and scale.

Desktop.variantHint: Integration category cards, 2-column or staggered 2-up list on desktop for readable scanning.
Desktop.notes: Use a clear list-card structure instead of dense multi-column grids. Group integration categories as separate cards with category title and comma-separated app examples. Keep this section highly scannable and avoid overcomplication. White background remains appropriate.
